name: eMudhra Ltd
title: eMudhra Ltd - 543533 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: eMudhra Q1 FY27 grew total income 28% to INR 1,925m with EBITDA margin 26.2%, but Trust token supply stalled on CCA ePass recertification, with ~INR 5-7 crore volume lost and Q2 top-line likely still soft.

summary.headline: eMudhra Q1 FY27 total income rose 28% YoY to INR 1,925 million, with EBITDA up 40% to INR 504 million at a 26.2% margin.
summary.overview: Total income grew 27.8% YoY to INR 1,925 million, of which about 13 points came from the Cryptas acquisition (about INR 200 million revenue). Enterprise Solutions grew about 50% YoY and made up 65% of income, while Trust Services declined temporarily as legacy token demand fell ahead of a September security-standard transition. PAT rose 28% to INR 320 million (16.6% margin), and management kept its FY27 guidance of 18% organic growth and 25% PAT growth unchanged.

segments.name: Enterprise Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,623 million, about 50% YoY growth and 65% of total income; organic product growth about 25% after Cryptas contribution, per management. Management cited higher margin mix from lower token sales.

segments.name: Trust Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 284 million with a temporary decline as partners destocked legacy tokens before a September transition. Management estimated INR 5-7 crore of token volume was lost; token gross margin is about 10%.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Growth of about 5% YoY, supported by new US customers; margins are roughly 18-20%, similar to historical levels.

segments.name: Cryptas (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR 20 crore in a seasonally weak quarter; first CertiNext sale to a German data center operator and first mSigner/PrimeSign deployment for an Austrian municipality. Management expects Cryptas to turn profitable in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 18% organic growth in total income and 25% PAT growth.
Management expects EBITDA margin around 25% and PAT margin around 16-16.5% going forward, as added sales hires weigh on costs.
Trust Service revenue likely stays lower in Q2 FY27 as legacy token demand remains weak; bottom-line impact described as limited given low token margins.
Three-year target (FY27-FY29) of doubling PAT, with about 18-20% organic revenue growth per year; Enterprise Solutions expected at 20-25% growth per year and Trust Services 15-20%.
UAE Trust Service (QTSP) licence expected around end of Q1 or start of Q2 FY27, after which launch is planned.
Expects the Cryptas loss to end in FY27 and the European subsidiary (BV) to be profitable this year; ROE expected to be maintained at about 14.5-15%.
capex_capacity: Token supply constrained: ePass token recertification by CCA submitted and largely complete, pending CCA action; management expects ePass certification by about September, after which volumes should recover.
New Innate token is certified but volumes are low because capacity is limited.

Cryptas integration of eMudhra's own CA and CLM IP replacing third-party products (such as Keyfactor) developed over the last six to seven months; this is intended to reduce cost and shift transfer pricing to India.
Added senior sales hires across geographies (USD 200,000-300,000 per person), which will weigh on near-term margins.
demand_pricing: Trust Services: partners destocked legacy tokens ahead of the September global transition to FIPS 140-3, which reduced volumes.

SecurePass in India: large bank or government deals typically start at INR 4-6 crore and can exceed INR 10 crore per bank for full PIM/PAM suites; compliance mandates from RBI-type regulators and SEBI-type regulators are cited as drivers.
US products: university federation (Common) onboarding is live, with about 1,000-1,500 certificates issued daily; IoT/PKI and SSL-expiry (47-day) demand are cited as pipeline drivers.
Agentic AI identity and signing is described as an early-stage opportunity; management said quantification is not possible yet and pilots are expected within about a year.
PrivaTrust consent-management modules are being piloted; a broader data discovery and classification suite is planned, with focus on India under the DPDP Act.

financial_highlights.change: About 13 points of 28% total income growth

qa_highlights.question: PrivaTrust cloud platform: is it live and what deployment opportunity exists in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Consent management is live with pilots and proofs of concept, with first wins expected soon. Additional data discovery and classification modules are to launch soon, with India the immediate focus because of the DPDP Act; management expects a clearer sizing in a quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: UAE QTSP licence timing and what the product is?
qa_highlights.answer: Final licence steps are underway, with completion expected around end of Q1 or start of Q2 FY27, after which launch follows. Management described it as an Aadhaar-eSign-type service, enterprise-oriented (sold mainly to banks and regulated entities) and complementary to emSigner in the UAE.

qa_highlights.question: Has the token supply issue been resolved and will Trust Services recover from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: ePass token recertification has been submitted and is largely done but pending CCA action; ePass certification is expected by about September. The new Innate token is certified but volumes are low due to limited capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Will Trust Services be hit in Q2 and is competition a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to partners not stocking legacy tokens ahead of the September expiry, with about INR 5-7 crore of volume lost against roughly INR 8-9 crore of normal token volume. Token gross margin is about 10%, so Q2 top-line stays lower but bottom-line impact is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why are international segment margins lower than India, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Services carry 18-20% margins versus 70-75% product gross margins; Cryptas (about INR 100 crore business) was unprofitable but is expected to turn profitable this year; senior sales hires cost USD 200,000-300,000 each. Management did not give a separate international margin target, guiding instead to 25% PAT growth and 18% top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated subsidiary loss of about INR 4 crore: what is it and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the European BV entity, which incurred legal expenses; Cryptas sits under BV. Management does not expect the loss to continue this year, with a senior salesperson in Rome chasing leads that could make BV profitable.

qa_highlights.question: US products outlook, pipeline and SecurePass growth drivers in India?
qa_highlights.answer: University federation (Common) onboarding is live with about 1,000-1,500 certificates issued daily. Management said enterprise growth of about 25% is being maintained. SecurePass wins are driven by RBI/SEBI-type authentication mandates; large bank or government deals start at INR 4-6 crore and can exceed INR 10 crore with full PIM/PAM suites.

qa_highlights.question: Cryptas integration: has in-sourcing cut losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Cryptas integration of eMudhra's own CA and CLM IP replacing third-party products like Keyfactor took about six to seven months. First wins (German data center CertiNext, Austrian municipality emSigner) validate the stack, and the cost saving comes through lower third-party cost and transfer pricing to India.

qa_highlights.question: Enterprise organic growth and Cryptas data-center opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Cryptas contributed about 25% of product growth, with about 25% organic growth in the product segment. Cryptas has marquee banking, insurance and oil and gas customers now treated as prospects for eMudhra products; data-center access security is seen as a large addressable market, not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Agentic AI opportunity and revenue today?
qa_highlights.answer: Early stage: conversations on agent risk, pilots expected within about a year, and no quantification yet. Agents would need digital signature certificate identities; no separate product, with CertiNext and SecurePass being strengthened instead.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margin bridge and sustainable range?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin rose on lower low-margin token sales and higher Enterprise mix. Management expects margins to hold around 25% EBITDA and 16-16.5% PAT as new senior sales hires add cost.

qa_highlights.question: FY30 vision and KPIs to track for doubling profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Three-year target (FY27-FY29) is to double PAT, with 18-20% organic revenue growth, Enterprise Solutions 20-25% and Trust Services 15-20%. The main tracked KPI is the order book multiple disclosed in the annual investor presentation.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't the shift to Enterprise lifted ROE/ROCE and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROE was about 14.5-15% last year and could be maintained at that level; reserves build up equity over time. It argued peers rarely exceed 25% EBITDA or 16% PAT margin and that the company keeps low borrowing by strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Service revenue share and Cryptas turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Services were about 19-20% of quarterly revenue, with historical margin profile maintained. Cryptas turnaround is attributed to first wins using eMudhra products instead of third-party products.

risks_watch: Trust Services: ePass recertification pending CCA action; management expects certification by about September, and volumes depend on it. Q2 FY27 top-line likely to stay weak.
Margin sustainability: senior sales hires at USD 200,000-300,000 each are expected to hold EBITDA near 25% and PAT near 16-16.5%.
Cryptas and BV: Cryptas expected to turn profitable in FY27; the European BV subsidiary had a consolidated loss of about INR 4 crore this quarter, linked to legal costs.
UAE QTSP licence: expected around end Q1/start Q2 FY27; launch timing and the enterprise go-to-market ramp remain unproven.
PrivaTrust and Agentic AI are early-stage with no revenue quantification; management said sizing may be possible in a quarter or two (PrivaTrust) or about a year (Agentic AI).
Legal matter with TI Infotech: no update; police have taken the company's statement. Management said the matter is in police hands with no timeline.
key_quotes: Of the 28% growth in total income, approximately 13% was contributed by the Cryptas acquisition, while the balance reflects healthy organic growth across our core businesses led by continued strength in our Enterprise Solution portfolio.
Our Trust Service business saw a temporary decline during the quarter following the transition to a new global security standard for digital signature tokens, which comes into effect in September.
We are not expecting the loss to continue in the current year.
Mostly by September, this ePass will be able to get certified, and then, again, it will start the token volume will increase.
It's not a retail product. It is enterprise -oriented in the UAE market.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Enterprise Solutions, international wins and the FY27 guidance, which was kept unchanged. Cautious and deliberately vague on Trust Services timing (dependent on CCA action), on quantifying new products (PrivaTrust, Agentic AI), and on the Cryptas and UAE timelines.

adds.what: Token supply constrained; ePass token recertification pending with CCA (not a capacity addition)

growth.why: FY27 guidance held at 18% organic total income growth and 25% PAT growth, plus a 2x PAT target over three years; backing is partial (Cryptas contribution, Enterprise Solutions ~50% growth, UAE QTSP licence and ePass recertification pending) with no specific capacity additions or contracted order values, and management described token capacity as very low.
